title: 'It's slow when the big ship is in'
description: A call-centre agent relays customer complaints in her own words (crawling, only some evenings, the big ship). Nobody names a mast. The radio specialist guesses ship radar, hedged, and the NOC maps the street to RAD-254. Tests hedged knowledge from a lay description: trust must stay 'hunch', and it binds to RAD-254 only.
subject: Customer calls: harbour area slow in the evenings

messages.text: Hei! not sure who to ask. I had six calls this week from people living by the harbour in Turku, they say the mobile internet is 'crawling' in the evenings
but not every evening. one lady says it's only when 'the big ship is in'
I told her it's probably her phone 😅 but she called twice
hmm. the harbour area is served from the hut on the quay, RAD-254 I think. what's the street?
Linnankatu. I don't know what a mast is, sorry 🙈
big ship... the ferry? ferries have radar
I saw something like this in Hamina years ago, a ship radar sweeping into a RU-400 sector. not sure it's the same here
customers said around 18 and again around 21
hm that fits. no promise. if someone is at the hut, try moving the RAD-254 sector to the other channel and see if the evenings get better
I'll note it for the hut. Outi can you ask the lady the exact time next time she calls?

items.summary: Evening slowdowns around the Turku harbour (about 18:00 and 21:00, when the ferry docks) may come from ship radar hitting the RAD-254 sector; unverified hunch. Try moving the sector to the other channel.

conditions.text: evening, when the ferry is in the harbour

items.diagnosis: possible ship radar interference in the RU-400 sector
items.action: At the hut, move the RAD-254 sector to the other channel and compare the evenings.
items.evidence: seq 7: 'not sure it's the same here' / seq 10: 'no promise'
